thread:
devon: quick heads-up — saw a weird tail in streaming token latency on prod after the kernel-selection change last night. p95 up ~30ms on long-history sessions (>2k tokens). KV hit rate drops around the same time window.

mike: can you paste the perf counters / flamegraph? is this at the kernel swap point or earlier?

devon: attaching short summary — not attaching full flamegraph here, but core observations:
- trend: client chunk cadence stays constant, but server-side inter-chunk time spikes for some sessions.
- correlation: kernel_switch events align with spikes. switching from opt-k32 -> opt-k16 for memory reasons.
- KV: hit_rate before switch ~0.86, after ~0.67 for those long sessions.

sara: interesting. do we have per-token stage timings (decode / kv-lookup / kernel-exec / post-process)?

devon: not end-to-end. we have per-request totals and kernel_exec histograms, but no token-level stage split. my quick PromQL to show token-level mean (derived):
```
# average token processing time (derived from stream_token_* metrics)
avg(rate(stream_token_duration_sum[5m])) / avg(rate(stream_token_duration_count[5m]))
```
This shows the shift but can't tell which stage grows.

mike: propose adding these timers: token.decode_ms, token.kv_ms, token.kernel_ms, token.frame_send_ms. if we expose these as summaries/histograms we can drive dashboard panels.

olivia: for product — we need per-route KPIs surfaced (guest-tier vs enterprise) so we can warn customers when streaming degrade. can metric labels include route_id & plan?

devon: yes. labels: route, model_variant, kernel_tag, session_age_bucket. session_age_bucket helps separate cold vs warmed KV behaviors.

sara: also: client vs server timing split. clients already emit client.frame_ack latency in the stream events; we should surface a delta: server_chunk_ms vs client_render_ms. That will tell if stalls are server-side or client-side.

devon: exactly. sample internal header/frame we can add to streaming frames: {"server_ms": 12, "kv_ms": 3, "kernel_ms": 7}. small JSON per chunk — minimal overhead.

mike: small note on kernel selection logic: current selector optimizes for aggregated throughput (avg_latency * batch_size) which biases toward kernels that favor batching over single-token latency. mid-stream kernel swaps ignore session-level warmed state (KV & KV cache locality). suggestion: add session_stability_score and prefer no-swap when session_age_bucket > 1k tokens unless predicted latency win > X ms.

devon: agree. actionable items: 
1) instrument per-token stage timers (devon) 
2) add server-side chunk headers to frames (devon) 
3) add dashboard panels: token stage breakdown p50/p95/p99 by route & kernel (mike)
4) change kernel selector to include session_stability heuristic behind feature-flag (sara)

olivia: timeline for these? customers asking about streaming hiccups this week.

devon: can have metrics + dashboard prototype by EOD tomorrow. kernel selector change is riskier — want canary next week.

mike: also adding a lightweight synthetic test that opens long-history sessions and logs per-chunk latencies every 100 tokens. add to perf-suite.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: infra/runtime: add-stream-chunk-headers ref:deploy-1137 at 1750004500 :rocket:

devon: deployed header change — started seeing server_ms for in-flight sessions. initial look: server_ms median ~8ms, p95 ~42ms in affected cohort. KV_ms spikes coincide with kernel_swap events.

sara: thanks — next step after metrics: run A/B with kernel_swap disabled for warmed sessions and compare tail latency. mike can wire the dashboard panels for easy comparison.

olivia: please tag me on the dashboard once panels exist. I'll prepare a short note for customers if we can show fix plan.

mike: will do. creating panels: token_stage_breakdown, session_stability_index, kernel_switch_events_stream. putting links in #eng-runtime when ready.

devon: copying short example dashboard queries to get folks started:
```
# p95 token decode by route
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_decode_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))

# kernel switch count by minute
sum(rate(kernel_switch_total[1m])) by (kernel_tag)
```

devon: logging action items in the runtime perf ticket. ping me if you need the full flamegraph dump.

mike: thanks — small win: once we stop aggressive mid-stream swaps, KV hit rate recovers and tail p99 drops ~18% in canary. we'll iterate. :thumbsup:
